but this didn't work. Can anyone please suggest a way to do this and combine standard latin text and greek letters in my facet_wrap titles?

Thank you
Hefin

Hi Lace,

I think you might be able to get what you want by restructuring your data
set. If it looks like this:

Ten <- data.frame(A_measure=c(rnorm(500, 10, 1),NA,NA),
 AB_measure=c(rep(NA,500),10,NA),
 B_measure=c(rep(NA,501),10),
 LowerQ=c(rep(NA,501),9),  # for example, but could obviously be the
quantile
 UpperQ=c(rep(NA,501),11),
 AB=c(rep("A",500),"AB","B") )

So that the data for each of A, B and AB are separate (as you want a
couple of types of graph and don't want an alpha applied to the AB point),
then:

p<-ggplot(Ten)+
geom_bar(aes(x=AB,y=B_measure,fill=AB),
 position=position_dodge(),
 stat="identity",width=0.5)+
geom_errorbar(aes(x=AB, ymin=LowerQ, ymax=UpperQ, color = AB),
 width=.1, position="dodge")+
 scale_fill_manual(values=c(NA,NA,"grey"))+
 scale_colour_manual(values=c(NA,NA,"black"))+
 geom_point(aes(x=AB,y=AB_measure),size=4,shape=4)+
 geom_point(aes(x=AB,y=A_measure),size=1,alpha=0.25,position="jitter")

should get you started.

While I've used geom_bar here, I agree with Roman that something like
geom_pointrange would be preferable to geom_bar.

Regards,
Ron.

​You are probably referring to the function defined in utilities-break.r <https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/f561c3448eb7b7addff0a9251e01cab08d3bb688/R/utilities-break.r#L92>?
"n" refers to "numbers" in the `equal` parameter. You should be able to deduce the rest from the code. Here's an example of usage:
>
> breaks <- function(x, equal, nbins = NULL, binwidth = NULL) {
>   equal <- match.arg(equal, c("numbers", "width"))
>   if ((!is.null(nbins) && !is.null(binwidth)) || (is.null(nbins) && is.null(binwidth))) {
>     stop("Specify exactly one of n and width")
>   }
>
>   rng <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE, finite = TRUE)
>   if (equal == "width") {
>     if (!is.null(binwidth)) {
>       fullseq(rng, binwidth)
>     } else {
>       seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = nbins + 1)
>     }
>   } else {
>     if (!is.null(binwidth)) {
>       probs <- seq(0, 1, by = binwidth)
>     } else {
>       probs <- seq(0, 1, length.out = nbins + 1)
>     }
>     stats::quantile(x, probs, na.rm = TRUE)
>   }
>
> }
>
> breaks(1:100, "numbers", nbins = 4)
> library(scales) # needs this because of scales::fullseq
> breaks(1:100, "width", binwidth = 5)

Cheers,
Roman

messages.subject: Re: Issue with Geom_Rect
messages.body_plain:
As a rule of thumb, you should _never_ include $ in your aes specifications.

Because of the rules of aesthetic inheritance, you also refer to the
variable y in the rect layer, and the rec dataframe doesn't contain a
variable called y.  This is easier to spot if you use white space and
indentation to layout your code:

ggplot(pix) +
  geom_point(aes(seq_along(y), y)) +
  geom_rect(
    aes(xmin = x1, xmax = x2, ymin = y1, ymax = y2)
    data = rec,
    color = 'grey',
    alpha = 0.2
  )
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1, 365, 730, 1095, 1460, 1825),
    labels = 2011:2016,
    limits = c(1, 2190)
  ) +
  theme_bw()

(I'm also extremely suspicious of your x axis - aligning arbitrary x
positions to years seems like a recipe for disaster)

Hadley

messages.body_plain:
Is there a ggplot alternative to using plotmath epression(atop( to get multiline axis titles?

Simply using \n allows lineheight control but looks horrible. Using expression(atop( looks nicer but has large in built lineheight that can't be changed with ggplot themes.

library(ggplot2)

# Multi line expression
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression(atop("line1", ~line^2)))

# Adjust line height to no avail
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression(atop("line1", ~line^2))) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.5, debug = TRUE))

# Insert extra line break with \n allows control of that line height
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression(atop("line1\n", ~line^2))) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.5, debug = TRUE))

# But we can't control the line break created by atop
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression(atop("line1\n", ~line^2))) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.00001, debug = TRUE))

# Removing atop causes other issues with centering...
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression("line1\n" ~line^2)) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(lineheight = 1, debug = TRUE))

Would this require arrange two searate text grobs for each line? Or is there a simpler way?
